guide.title: Hazardous Materials & Radiation
guide.lead: Don't become a casualty. Approach from upwind and uphill, stop at a distance, identify the substance from placards and the Emergency Response Guidebook, and work in the cold zone. Strip patients – removing clothing removes most contamination – and remember that irradiated patients are not radioactive.

steps.title: Upwind, uphill, upstream
steps.text: Stop well back: at least 100 m (330 feet) until the guidebook gives a distance.

steps.title: Identify from afar
steps.text: Placards, UN numbers, labels, shipping papers, binoculars. Look them up in the Emergency Response Guidebook.

steps.title: Isolate and deny entry
steps.text: Keep people out; call hazmat; report with METHANE.

steps.title: Zones
steps.text: Hot (contamination), warm (decontamination), cold (treatment and staging). EMS works in the cold zone unless trained and equipped.

sections.title: PPE levels
rows: Fully encapsulated, vapour-tight suit with SCBA
SCBA with a splash suit: highest breathing protection
Air-purifying respirator and splash suit: known agent, enough oxygen

steps.title: Strip
steps.text: Removing clothing removes most contamination (up to 90%). Bag it.

steps.title: Rinse
steps.text: Plenty of lukewarm, low-pressure water; soap for oily agents. Dry powders: brush off first.

steps.title: Life before decon
steps.text: Airway, bleeding control and antidotes can't wait – done by protected staff.

sections.title: Common toxic exposures
rows: SLUDGEM: secretions, sweating, small pupils, slow pulse, twitching
Atropine until secretions dry; pralidoxime; benzodiazepine for seizures
Sudden collapse, seizures, high lactate, little cyanosis
Oxygen; hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV over 15 minutes (child 70 mg/kg)
Eye and airway burning, cough, wheeze

sections.title: Radiation
rows: Exposed but carries no radioactive material: no risk to you
Radioactive material on or in them: strip and wash, but treat life threats first
Very high dose, likely fatal (over 8 Gy)

items.label: METHANE report
items.sub: First report from a hazmat scene

quiz.q: Truck crash with a greenish-yellow cloud and bleach smell; the driver is coughing near the truck. You:
options: Stop upwind and uphill at a distance, identify from afar, call hazmat
Approach from downwind to read the placard
Treat the driver where he is
quiz.explanation: Likely chlorine; don't become a casualty.

quiz.q: Your role in the warm zone helping decontaminate patients exposed to a known agent with adequate oxygen. Usual PPE?
options: Level C: splash suit with air-purifying respirator (Level B if unknown)
quiz.explanation: Level C needs a known agent.

quiz.q: Sprayed with farm pesticide: drooling, tearing, vomiting, diarrhoea, small pupils, wheeze, slow pulse. Treatment?
options: Decontaminate (protected), atropine until secretions dry, pralidoxime, oxygen

quiz.q: Firefighter from a smoky fire: confused, seizure, low BP, SpO₂ normal. Besides CO, suspect:
quiz.explanation: Smoke contains cyanide from burning plastics.
Radioactive placards are yellow and white with a trefoil.

quiz.q: Subway chemical release: people streaming out coughing, some collapsed inside. You:
options: Set up triage and decontamination upwind outside; don't enter without proper PPE
quiz.explanation: Contaminated patients spread the hazard to hospitals.

quiz.q: Worker splashed with hydrogen cyanide, unconscious and seizing. You:
options: Protected staff remove him and decontaminate; oxygen and hydroxocobalamin
Large amounts of water to drink

quiz.q: A vial of radioactive iodine broke in a lab; no visible contamination on the worker. Most accurate?
options: Survey him; if not contaminated he's simply irradiated and poses no risk

quiz.q: The single most effective decontamination step:
Vomiting within 10 minutes of radiation exposure suggests:
options: A very high, likely fatal dose
quiz.explanation: Earlier vomiting means a higher dose.

quiz.q: Placard with a skull and crossbones on white:
quiz.explanation: Red and white stripes are flammable solids.

flashcards.question: Hazmat zones
flashcards.answer: Hot (contamination; trained entry only), warm (decontamination), cold (treatment, command, staging). EMS treats in the cold zone.

flashcards.question: Most effective decontamination step
flashcards.answer: Remove the clothing (up to 90% of contamination), then rinse with plenty of low-pressure lukewarm water.

flashcards.question: Irradiation vs contamination
flashcards.answer: Irradiated: exposed, not radioactive – no risk to you. Contaminated: radioactive material on or in them – decontaminate, but treat life threats first.

flashcards.question: SLUDGEM
flashcards.answer: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI upset, Emesis, Miosis – cholinergic crisis from organophosphates or nerve agents. Watch the killer Bs: bronchorrhoea, bronchospasm, bradycardia.

flashcards.question: Nerve agent antidotes
flashcards.answer: Atropine (dries secretions, titrate to dry chest), pralidoxime (reactivates the enzyme), benzodiazepine for seizures.

flashcards.question: Cyanide antidote
flashcards.answer: Hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV over 15 minutes (child 70 mg/kg). Turns skin and urine red.

flashcards.question: Toxic gas placard
flashcards.answer: White with a skull and crossbones (class 2.3). Flammable gas: red. Non-flammable gas: green.

flashcards.question: Four PPE levels
flashcards.answer: A: vapour-tight with SCBA. B: SCBA with splash suit. C: air-purifying respirator, known agent. D: work uniform.

flashcards.question: Time to vomiting after radiation
flashcards.answer: Within 10 minutes: likely fatal dose. Within 1–2 hours: moderate (about 2–4 Gy). After 2 hours or none: low dose (under 2 Gy).

flashcards.question: Emergency Response Guidebook
flashcards.answer: The orange book on every response vehicle: look up UN numbers or names for hazards, isolation distances and first aid.

critical.scenario: Factory 'chemical exposure': a worker in a stained suit walks toward your ambulance carrying an unlabelled container, coughing.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Stop him at a distance, tell him to put the container down, stay upwind, isolate the area, call hazmat; decontaminate before treatment
Take the container to identify it
Enter the building to find others

critical.explanation: A contaminated ambulance is out of service.
critical.kpi: Recognizes hazmat red flags and prevents secondary contamination

critical.scenario: City park: about 20 people vomiting, coughing, with watery eyes; some seizing. You have no hazmat PPE.
critical.question: Plan?

options.t: Stay upwind at a distance, declare a mass-casualty chemical incident, call hazmat, direct walking patients upwind to a safe spot, prepare antidotes and triage after decontamination
Rush in to treat the seizing

critical.explanation: Suspect a nerve agent: miosis and secretions help confirm.
critical.kpi: Manages a chemical mass-casualty incident safely

critical.scenario: Postal facility 'white powder': patients have been stripped, washed and are well. One is anxious and asks if he will die.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Reassure, check vital signs, record his details for public health follow-up; most such incidents are hoaxes, but the substance will be tested

options.f: Anthrax doesn't spread person to person.

options.t: Repeat decontamination with bleach on skin

critical.explanation: Fear spreads faster than agents: clear communication matters.
critical.kpi: Manages psychological impact after a suspected biological exposure
